heading.en: One frog or a population of frogs?

hook.en: A single frog is born and dies, but it has no birth rate. Birth rate, death rate and sex ratio belong only to a *population*, a group of individuals of one species in an area.

say.en: A single frog is born and dies, but it has no birth rate. Birth rate, death rate and sex ratio belong only to a population, a group of individuals of one species in an area. In this lesson: Define a population and its attributes.
Calculate per capita birth and death rates.
Interpret age pyramids and ways of measuring population density.

title.en: Birth rate, death rate and sex ratio

body.en: In nature we rarely find isolated single individuals of a species; most live in groups in a well-defined geographical area, share or compete for similar resources, and potentially interbreed: such a group is a population. A population has attributes that an individual does not. *Birth rate* and death rate are expressed per capita: if a pond had 20 lotus plants last year and 8 new plants were added by reproduction, the birth rate is 8/20 = 0.4 offspring per lotus per year. If 4 of a laboratory population of 40 fruit flies died during a week, the death rate is 4/40 = 0.1 individuals per fruit fly per week. Sex ratio is another attribute: for example, 60 per cent of a population may be females and 40 per cent males.

points.en: *Population*: same species, same area, can interbreed
Birth and *death rates* are per capita rates
Lotus: 8/20 = 0.4 per year; fruit flies: 4/40 = 0.1 per week
*Sex ratio*: proportion of females and males

narration.en: Birth and death rates are per capita: 8 new lotus plants in a pond of 20 is a birth rate of 0.4 per plant per year, and 4 deaths among 40 fruit flies is a death rate of 0.1 per fly per week. Sex ratio is the proportion of females to males.

say.en: Birth and death rates are per capita rates.
Lotus: 8 over 20 equals 0.4 per year; fruit flies: 4 over 40 equals 0.1 per week.
Sex ratio: proportion of females and males.
A population has attributes an individual does not have. Birth rate is the number born divided by the population size: a per capita rate.
Twenty lotus plants gave eight new plants in a year: birth rate 0.4 per lotus per year. Four of forty fruit flies died in a week: death rate 0.1 per fly per week.
Stack the age groups as bars and you get an age pyramid. A broad base means a growing population, a bell is stable, and an urn shape with a narrow base is declining.
Density can be measured by numbers, per cent cover or biomass. For tigers in a reserve we count pugmarks and faecal pellets instead.

body.en: A population at any time has individuals of different ages. When the age distribution (per cent individuals of a given age or age group) is plotted, the result is an age pyramid; for humans it also shows the age distribution of males and females. The three age groups are pre-reproductive, reproductive and post-reproductive. The shape of the pyramid shows the growth status: expanding (triangular, broad base: growing population), stable (bell-shaped) and declining (urn-shaped, narrow base). Population size, technically *population density* (N), need not be counted as numbers every time. Per cent cover or biomass is a more meaningful measure when there are a few huge trees and many small plants. Relative density is often enough: the number of fish caught per trap. Tiger census in national parks and tiger reserves is often based on pugmarks and faecal pellets.

points.en: Expanding: triangular; stable: bell-shaped; declining: urn-shaped
*Density* by count, per cent cover, biomass or relative density

narration.en: An age pyramid with a broad base shows a growing population, a bell shape a stable one, and an urn shape a declining one. Density can be measured by counting, by per cent cover or biomass, or relatively, for example fish caught per trap or tiger pugmarks.

problem.en: A village pond had 250 frogs at the start of the year. During the year 75 froglets joined the adult population by reproduction and 25 frogs died. Find the per capita birth rate and death rate.

answer.en: Birth rate 0.3 and death rate 0.1 per frog per year.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A village pond had 250 frogs at the start of the year. During the year 75 froglets joined the adult population by reproduction and 25 frogs died. Find the per capita birth rate and death rate.

say.en: Let us work through this together. A village pond had 250 frogs at the start of the year. During the year 75 froglets joined the adult population by reproduction and 25 frogs died. Find the per capita birth rate and death rate.
Birth rate equals number born divided by population equals 75 divided by 250 equals 0.3.
Death rate equals number died divided by population equals 25 divided by 250 equals 0.1.
Units: per frog per year.
So the answer is Birth rate 0.3 and death rate 0.1 per frog per year.

body.en: A wide base means many young: the population will grow (triangle). Equal widths: stable (bell). A narrow base: few young, the population will shrink (urn).
